title_en: Zhi Guoxiang v. Tax Authority — dispute over tax administrative penalty
keywords_en: Administrative; tax administrative penalty; second instance; intermediate people's court; Henan Province; natural person; state organ; Product Tax Regulations (Draft); General Principles of Civil Law; Civil Procedure Law (for Trial Implementation); determination of taxpayer; legality of tax penalty; administrative compensation; reversal; brick kiln contracting; subcontract contract; product tax collection dispute; tax authority freezing brick sales; administrative penalty
full_text_en:
Zhi Guoxiang v. Tax Administrative Penalty Case

Appellant (Plaintiff at First Instance): Zhi Guoxiang, male, 56 years old, farmer of Shangdian Township, Biyang County, Henan Province.

Agent ad litem: Zhang Ping'an and Chen Jingxiang, lawyers of Zhumadian Prefecture Economic Law Firm, Henan Province.

Appellee (Defendant at First Instance): Zhumadian Prefecture Tax Bureau, Henan Province.

Legal Representative: Sun Dingfang, Director of Zhumadian Prefecture Tax Bureau.

Agent ad litem: Yang Mingxin, Deputy Section Chief of Biyang County Tax Bureau, Henan Province.

Agent ad litem: Bi Xianxing, lawyer of Nanyang Prefecture Law Firm.

The appellant, Zhi Guoxiang, appealed to the Zhumadian Prefecture Intermediate People's Court, Henan Province, against the judgment of the Biyang County People's Court, Henan Province, (1988) Bi Fa Xing Zi No. 01, in a tax dispute case. The Zhumadian Prefecture Intermediate People's Court, Henan Province, lawfully formed a collegial panel and, after a public hearing, found the following facts:

There was a 16-kiln brick and tile yard in Xianghe Township, Biyang County, Henan Province, which was a township-run collectively-owned enterprise. In 1984, Fu Xincun, a farmer of that township, signed a contract with the township people's government for the undertaking of the enterprise. The contract stipulated: the township government was Party A, and Fu Xincun was Party B. Party A leased the brick and tile yard to Party B and provided factory buildings, premises, and brick-making machinery; Party B was responsible for operation and management, bore the taxes payable by the enterprise, and paid Party A a contracting fee of RMB 5,500; the contract period was one year, from January 1984 to the end of December of that year. After Fu Xincun undertook the enterprise, he, as the lessor, signed a brick-making technical contract with Zhi Guoxiang, a farmer of Shangdian Township. The contract stipulated: Fu Xincun was Party A, and Zhi Guoxiang was Party B; the contract period was one year; Party A provided factory buildings, machinery and other equipment and investment, and Party B produced 2 million finished bricks for Party A, with each brick sold at a price of RMB 0.05. Party A extracted RMB 0.015 per brick (including taxes payable, purchase of handcarts and covers), and Party B received RMB 0.035 per brick (including purchase of diesel oil, coal and other fuels, workers' wages, and tool repair costs). If Party B produced less than 2 million bricks, Party A extracted RMB 0.018 per brick; if less than 1.5 million bricks, Party A extracted RMB 0.02 per brick. If Party B produced more than 2 million bricks, Party A extracted RMB 0.012 per brick for the excess. After the contract took effect, Zhi Guoxiang commenced production. The contract was performed for eight months, during which Zhi Guoxiang produced 680,000 finished bricks, equivalent to RMB 34,000. Of this amount, Zhi Guoxiang received RMB 3,200, and the remainder was collected and kept by Party A.

In November 1984, the Xianghe Township Tax Office notified Zhi Guoxiang to pay the product tax on brick production. Zhi Guoxiang stated that the contract provided that Party A should bear the tax. However, the tax office insisted that the tax should be paid by Zhi Guoxiang and persisted in collecting it from him, leading to a dispute. Because Zhi Guoxiang insisted that the tax should be paid by Party A, the tax office sent personnel to take 60,000 bricks produced by Zhi Guoxiang to offset the tax in kind, but they were prevented by workers from removing them. The tax office immediately announced the freezing of the bricks produced by Zhi Guoxiang, to be sold only after the tax was paid. Thereafter, Zhi Guoxiang appealed to the Biyang County Tax Bureau on the grounds that he should not be liable for tax and that the township tax office had obstructed his production and sale of bricks, but the issue was not resolved. On August 7, 1986, the Biyang County Tax Bureau issued a written penalty decision: 1. Zhi Guoxiang, as the producer of machine-made bricks, was the taxpayer and should pay product tax of RMB 3,400 according to law; 2. Zhi Guoxiang failed to register for tax purposes as required, and was fined RMB 500. Zhi Guoxiang, dissatisfied with this decision, applied for administrative reconsideration to the higher-level tax authority. After reconsideration, the Zhumadian Prefecture Tax Bureau still held that Zhi Guoxiang was the taxpayer. Zhi Guoxiang, dissatisfied with the reconsideration decision of the Zhumadian Prefecture Tax Bureau, filed a lawsuit with the Biyang County People's Court.

The court of first instance held that after undertaking the Xianghe Brick and Tile Kiln Yard, Zhi Guoxiang hired workers and organized production, and was the producer. According to Articles 1 and 2 of the Product Tax Regulations of the People's Republic of China (Draft), Zhi Guoxiang was the taxpayer and should pay tax. Judgment: Affirmed the reconsideration decision of the Henan Zhumadian Prefecture Tax Bureau and dismissed the plaintiff's complaint.

Zhi Guoxiang, dissatisfied with the first-instance judgment, appealed to the Zhumadian Prefecture Intermediate People's Court, stating: The contract I signed with Party A stipulated that I would produce 2 million finished bricks for Party A and receive remuneration on a proportional basis. The contractor of the brick and tile yard, Fu Xincun, exercised the rights of production planning, operation, and management of the enterprise and bore all taxes of the enterprise. Therefore, I am not the taxpayer. Due to the illegal exercise of power by the tax authorities, the contract between Party A and me could not be performed, causing economic losses, which should be compensated. The first-instance judgment found the facts incorrectly and requested its reversal.

Upon trial, the Zhumadian Prefecture Intermediate People's Court held: The taxpayers stipulated in Article 1 of the Product Tax Regulations (Draft) include natural persons and legal persons. The Xianghe Township Brick and Tile Kiln Yard was a township enterprise of collectively-owned nature. After the enterprise was contracted out, it was clearly stipulated that the contractor should bear the taxes. Later, although the contractor subcontracted the brick production quota to Zhi Guoxiang, the contract still stated that the contractor of the brick and tile kiln yard should bear the taxes. During the period when Zhi Guoxiang was making bricks, the contractor Fu Xincun exercised the rights of production and operation management over the sale of products and financial revenues and expenditures of the kiln yard. Therefore, the product tax for the brick and tile kiln yard in 1984 should be paid by that enterprise. The first-instance judgment's determination that Zhi Guoxiang was the taxpayer was erroneous. Due to the tax authority's erroneous identification of the taxpayer and the adoption of measures such as freezing brick sales and stopping production, Zhi Guoxiang suffered certain economic losses. In accordance with Article 121 of the General Principles of Civil Law of the People's Republic of China, which states that "If a state organ or a functionary thereof infringes upon the lawful rights and interests of a citizen or legal person in the performance of their duties, it shall bear civil liability," and Article 151, paragraph 1, item (2) of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China (for Trial Implementation), the Zhumadian Prefecture Intermediate People's Court rendered the following judgment on November 23, 1988:

1. Set aside the judgment of the Biyang County People's Court, (1988) Bi Fa Xing Zi No. 01;
2. Set aside the penalty decision of the Zhumadian Prefecture Tax Bureau against Zhi Guoxiang;
3. The Zhumadian Prefecture Tax Bureau shall compensate Zhi Guoxiang for his economic losses in the amount of RMB 1,000.
